G. Annual Report on Low-Moderate Income Housing Asset Fund for Fiscal Year 2024-25
Recommended Action

1. Adopt a finding of no possibility of significant effect pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines;

Direct the City Manager to present the independent audit of the Low- and Moderate-Income Housing Asset Fund to the City Council upon completion of the independent audit of the City’s Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) and authorize the City Manager to post the results of the audit on the City's website after presentation to City Council.

A. Approval of Negotiations for Upcoming Major Events New Item Received. 8/6/2026
Recommended Action
Staff recommend that the City Council:
1. Make findings that approval of an exclusive negotiating agreement (ENA), letter of intent (LOI), or a term sheet for real estate negotiation purposes do not constitute an approval of a project requiring CEQA review because they do not commit the City to any specific terms of a project; and that the City’s actions contemplated in this report constitute planning and feasibility studies which are exempt from CEQA pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 1526 2 .
2. Authorize the City Manager to execute a Letter of Intent (LOI) term sheet and negotiate and execute a license agreement subject to CEQA compliance, with the French National Olympic and Sport Committee to host a hospitality house activation at the Annenberg Community Beach House during the 2028 Summer Olympic Games.
3. Authorize the City Manager to execute a term sheet (Term Sheet)  and negotiate the terms of a license agreement subject to CEQA compliance with LOIDL LLC dba Hochsitz to host a Nations Villag e to include International Olympic Committee (IOC) satellite broadcast center, National Olympic Committee hospitality house, and brand hospitality house activation at Crescent Bay Park and portions of Lot 4 South during the LA28 Summer Olympic Games.
4. Authorize the City Manager to execute an Exclusive Negotiation Agreement (ENA) and negotiate the terms of a license agreement subject to CEQA compliance with ESPN Productions Inc. to explore a multi-day fan festival experience and international broadcast studio in conjunction with a major sporting event at SoFi Stadium in winter 2027.
5. Award RFP#462 to Goldenvoice LLC, to assess the viability of developing a music festival event on Santa Monica Beach in the fall of 2026 and authorize the City Manager to enter into an Exclusive Negotiation Agreement and negotiate the terms of a license agreement subject to CEQA compliance.
6. Authorize the City Manager to execute an Exclusive Negotiation Agreement (ENA) and negotiate the terms of a license agreement subject to CEQA compliance with Anheuser-Busch to explore a World Cup fan festival experience at the Santa Monica Pier in June 2026.

12. PUBLIC HEARINGS
A. Approval of Establishment of a Self-Certification Pilot Program and Introduction and First Reading of Ordinances to (1) Amend Santa Monica Municipal Code Chapter 8.108 to revise the Construction and Demolition Material Recycling Compliance Process and to transition from a deposit-based system to a fine-based enforcement approach, and (2) Establish Interim Zoning Regulations Updating Applicability Thresholds and Standards for Resource and Recycling Room Dimensions; and Adopt a Resolution of Intention to Amend the Text Section 9.21.130 of the Zoning Ordinance Related to Resource Recovery and Recycling Standards
Recommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council:
1. Adopt a finding of Statutory Exemption from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Government Code Section 15061(b)(3).
2. Introduce for First Reading an Ordinance amending Santa Monica Municipal Code Chapter 8.108, Subpart B, to amend the construction and demolition material recycling compliance process and to transition from a deposit-based system to a fine-based enforcement approach.
3. Introduce for First Reading an Interim Zoning Ordinance updating applicability thresholds and standards for resource and recycling room dimensions set forth in Santa Monica Municipal Code Section 9.21.130 in order to further economic recovery efforts by facilitating a self-certification building permit program.
4. Adopt a Resolution of Intention directing the Planning Commission to initiate amendments to the text of Section 9.21.130 of the City’s Zoning Ordinance to update applicability thresholds and resource and recycling room dimensions in order to further economic recovery efforts by facilitating a self-certification building permit program.
